facts.text: NBC News reported thieves have stolen more than $100 million in data center freight since June 2026.
facts.check_note: Page quotes NBC News: thieves 'made away with more than $100 million in data center freight', and the summary says since June.

facts.text: Thieves hack freight brokers' accounts, post fake shipments to attract real bids, and send malicious links to trucking companies; once clicked, they take over accounts and bid on real shipments.
facts.check_note: Matches the Ars Technica summary on the page.

facts.text: Real drivers are sometimes hired unknowingly to pick up cargo; in other cases fake driver's licenses place accomplices as drivers.
facts.check_note: Page says a real driver is sometimes hired unknowingly, and other times fake licenses get accomplices hired.

facts.text: In one of the largest thefts, GPS tracking coordinates were spoofed to avoid digital monitoring.
facts.check_note: Page says tracking coordinates were spoofed in one of the largest thefts.

facts.text: Targets include servers, fiber-optic cables, memory chips, copper wire and bitcoin mining machines.
facts.check_note: Page lists servers, fiber-optic cables, computer memory chips, copper wires and bitcoin mining machines.

facts.text: In two of the largest thefts, nothing was recovered, and off-duty police officers hired as escorts were targeted in hit-and-run incidents.
facts.check_note: Page says that in two of the largest thefts none of the equipment was found and off-duty cops hired as escorts were targeted in hit-and-runs.

facts.text: A Los Angeles County Sheriff's sergeant told NBC this is how most of these thefts are now carried out, unlike earlier mostly opportunistic highway thefts.
facts.check_note: LASD Sgt. Pantoja told NBC 'that's how most of it is being done', a shift from largely opportunistic thefts.

facts.text: In Los Angeles County, police recovered data center cooling equipment bound for Deepcool AI, mixed with nicotine pouches, TVs and cosmetics.
facts.check_note: Page describes the LASD case with cooling equipment bound for Deepcool AI recovered among nicotine pouches, TVs, cosmetics and other goods.

facts.text: Cook County Sheriff's Office estimated two stolen loads held about $300,000 in copper wire and about $1 million in data center power equipment.
facts.check_note: Cook County Sheriff's Office estimates: $300,000 in copper wire spools and about $1 million in modular power equipment, in two stolen freights.

facts.text: Scott Cornell of SPG Cargo & Logistics confirmed $110.6 million in known reported data center and high-tech cargo thefts since June 3; individual cases ranged from $2 million to $38 million.
facts.check_note: Page supports $110.6M in known reported thefts since June 3 and individual cases from $2M to $38M, per Cornell. The 'as of Aug. 14, 2026' date is not on the page.
facts.original: Scott Cornell of SPG Cargo & Logistics put known data center freight thefts at $110.6 million since June 3 (as of Aug. 14, 2026); individual cases ranged from $2 million to $38 million.

facts.text: Thieves deliberately crashed into security escorts on two high-value tech loads and the drivers kept going; Cornell linked both to carrier verification failures and said drivers 'weren't properly vetted'.
facts.check_note: Page says thieves intentionally crashed into escorts on two thefts, the drivers kept going, Cornell linked both to carrier verification failures, and he said the drivers weren't properly vetted.

facts.text: Cornell estimated six or seven of every 10 stolen US loads now leave the country.
facts.check_note: Cornell estimated six or seven out of every 10 stolen US loads now leave the country.

facts.text: Overhaul says cargo thieves stole more than $150 million in AI equipment in 2026, and thefts of data center equipment, chips and computing components rose 34% since 2024.
facts.check_note: Page says Overhaul reports more than $150M in AI equipment stolen this year, and a 34% increase since 2024. The article is dated October 2026.

facts.text: A flagship AI server rack costs about $3 million, per Overhaul, so one truckload can hold eight figures in value.
facts.check_note: Overhaul's report says a flagship AI server rack costs roughly $3 million, so one truckload routinely carries eight figures.

facts.text: Overhaul says deception (not force) was used in 92% of thefts involving high-value technology shipments, a shift 'from force to fraud'.
facts.check_note: Page says Overhaul noted a shift from 'force to fraud', with deception tactics used in 92% of high-value technology shipment thefts.

facts.text: Arizona passed a law in July 2026 creating a statewide cargo theft task force and enhanced sentences for fraud-based theft; California, Michigan and Tennessee also passed cargo theft laws in 2026.
facts.check_note: Page says Arizona passed the law in July, with a statewide task force and enhanced sentences. California, Michigan and Tennessee approved cargo theft legislation 'this year', and the article is dated 2026.

facts.text: Cornell recommends secure digital bills of lading and thorough carrier and driver checks, noting paper bills of lading let thieves alter product descriptions.
facts.check_note: Cornell encouraged secure digital bills of lading and carrier and driver verification, and identified paper bills of lading as a weakness because thieves can replace product descriptions.
